description: Public TLP:CLEAR Chinese-language threat reports used to evaluate IOC extraction. PDFs are not committed: zh-cn copies come from github.com/CyberMonitor/APT_CyberCriminal_Campagin_Collections (commit cbf136e24f5d2a4d89619580455aae8b9b0aeadb, blob SHA-1 below); zh-tw files were downloaded by the maintainer. The original URL is the publisher's own page; 'url_source' says how it was established.

fields.format: "pdf" (the default) or "html"; the source file is eval-data/<set>/<format>/<id>.<format> unless 'source' names it
fields.html_source: for a web page: "server" (the HTML the server sent, preferred) or "rendered" (the DOM saved from a browser, used only when the server's HTML lacks the content), with the reason
fields.http_charset: for a web page: the charset of the Content-Type header it was served with, if known; it takes precedence over a <meta> charset
fields.attachments: files in eval-data/<set>/attachments/ whose text follows the page text, when the indicators are only there (PDF read with pypdf, a web page converted like a page, anything else as UTF-8 text); their SHA-256 is recorded
fields.appendix: start and end markers of the IOC appendix; the start marker must occur once in the text, or 'start_occurrence' (1-based) says which occurrence begins the appendix
fields.truth_corrections: hand corrections of the ground truth (add, remove, ambiguous), each with a reason

text_conversion.pdf: pypdf (version in requirements.txt and in each results file): page.extract_text() for each page, joined with line breaks; page headers and footers kept
text_conversion.html: evaluate.py: decode_html (strict decoding: byte-order mark, valid UTF-8, charset declared in the HTTP header, then in <meta>, then Big5 as cp950; nothing decoded leniently) and HtmlText (Python standard library html.parser; visible text of the whole <body>, navigation and footer included; block elements on their own lines, table cells separated by TAB; source line breaks folded to spaces; soft hyphens deleted; hidden content kept and counted; attributes not read). The rules are in their docstrings. html.parser's handling of malformed markup changed in Python security releases, so the Python version is recorded with each conversion; the fixture tests in tests/test_research_html.py pass on 3.11.4 (the evaluation environment) and on 3.11.17 to 3.14.
text_conversion.choice: When a report exists as both PDF and web page, only the one at original_url is evaluated.

The domain tables wrap long names inside narrow cells, and the layout puts a '-' at every wrap. Rule 1: a '-' next to a dot at a wrap ('serveuser.-' + 'com', '163mailboxdownload-' + '.servehttp.com') cannot be part of a name, so it was inserted: the name is added without it and the fragments the line rules produced are removed. Rule 2: 'dynamic-' + 'dns.net' is the dynamic DNS provider dynamic-dns.net, which cn02 lists unwrapped, so that '-' is kept. Any other '-' at a wrap may or may not belong to the name; those entries are left out of the ground truth like masked ones, both readings are listed under 'ambiguous', and an extracted value equal to either reading is counted neither right nor wrong.
